title: Where a Fabric Spark setting actually lives: the five configuration layers
purpose: Fabric Spark configuration layers. Capacity layer; Workspace Spark settings; Environment item; Notebook session configure; Running session conf set; Why a setting does not stick.
accessibleSummary: Fabric Spark configuration layers. Capacity layer; Workspace Spark settings; Environment item; Notebook session configure; Running session conf set; Why a setting does not stick.
longDescription: Fabric Spark configuration layers. Capacity layer; Workspace Spark settings; Environment item; Notebook session configure; Running session conf set; Why a setting does not stick.

nodes.label: 1. Capacity
nodes.summary: The capacity SKU and its switches bound every workspace beneath it.
nodes.detail: The capacity SKU and its switches bound every workspace beneath it.
nodes.whyItMatters: The capacity SKU and its switches bound every workspace beneath it.

evidence.note: Capacity SKUs map to Spark vCores at two vCores per capacity unit and cap starter pool size.

processing: Bound available Spark vCores and pool maxima
outputs: A ceiling for every workspace on the capacity
drill.example: An F64 capacity provides 128 Spark vCores of base compute.
failureModes: A pool configured beyond the SKU ceiling cannot reach its stated maximum.

nodes.label: 2. Workspace Spark settings
nodes.summary: Workspace Spark settings own the default pool and the runtime version.
nodes.detail: Workspace Spark settings own the default pool and the runtime version.
nodes.whyItMatters: Workspace Spark settings own the default pool and the runtime version.

evidence.note: The runtime version is changed at Workspace Settings, Data Engineering/Science, Spark settings.
Starter pools use Medium nodes with autoscale and dynamic executor allocation enabled by default.

processing: Select default pool and runtime version
outputs: Defaults inherited by items in the workspace
drill.example: Switching the workspace runtime applies from the next session, not to a running one.
failureModes: Changing the runtime here silently drops settings incompatible with the target runtime.

nodes.label: 3. Environment item
nodes.summary: The Environment item is the right home for team-wide Spark properties and libraries.
nodes.detail: The Environment item is the right home for team-wide Spark properties and libraries.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Environment item is the right home for team-wide Spark properties and libraries.

evidence.note: The Environment item carries a runtime override, Spark properties and libraries, and is published before use.
The Environment is the right home for team-wide session-start settings and the native execution toggle.

processing: Set Spark properties, libraries and compute overrides
outputs: Consistent configuration for every attached notebook
drill.example: The native execution toggle and ANSI decision are recorded here rather than per notebook.
failureModes: Libraries must be re-added and published after a runtime move, or jobs fail to import them.

nodes.label: 4. Notebook or job session
nodes.summary: A %%configure cell sets session-start scope before the session exists.
nodes.detail: A %%configure cell sets session-start scope before the session exists.
nodes.whyItMatters: A %%configure cell sets session-start scope before the session exists.

evidence.note: Session-start settings belong in a %%configure cell or the Environment's Spark properties, not in code.

processing: Apply session-start configuration before the session starts
outputs: A session with the requested shape
drill.example: A memory-heavy notebook requests a larger executor shape for that run only.
failureModes: If the workspace forbids item-level compute customization, the request is ignored.

nodes.label: 5. Running session
nodes.summary: spark.conf.set reaches only runtime-mutable keys on a live session.
nodes.detail: spark.conf.set reaches only runtime-mutable keys on a live session.
nodes.whyItMatters: spark.conf.set reaches only runtime-mutable keys on a live session.

evidence.note: Adaptive settings, shuffle partitions and the broadcast threshold are runtime-adjustable query settings.
Only runtime-mutable keys can be set from code once a session exists.

drill.example: Raising the broadcast threshold for one known-small dimension mid-notebook.
failureModes: Setting executor memory here has no effect and produces no error.

nodes.label: A lower layer overrode it
nodes.summary: Precedence flows downward, so a lower layer can override a higher one.
nodes.detail: Precedence flows downward, so a lower layer can override a higher one.
nodes.whyItMatters: Precedence flows downward, so a lower layer can override a higher one.

evidence.note: Precedence flows downward and the debug rule is to check whether a lower layer is overriding the setting.

outputs: The effective value actually in force
drill.example: A notebook configure cell wins over the Environment property it contradicts.
failureModes: A stray notebook setting silently overrides a carefully governed Environment default.

nodes.label: It was set too late to matter
nodes.summary: Configuration applied after the session exists is silently dropped.
nodes.detail: Configuration applied after the session exists is silently dropped.
nodes.whyItMatters: Configuration applied after the session exists is silently dropped.

evidence.note: In Fabric the session already exists before the first cell, so a SparkSession builder returns the existing session and drops every chained config.

inputs: Configuration applied in code after session start
outputs: A job running with unintended settings
drill.example: A builder chain setting executor memory has no effect and raises no error.
controls: Move the setting to %%configure or the Environment
failureModes: The job is tuned on paper and untuned in reality, with nothing in the logs to say so.

edges.label: Workspace default is overridden per Environment
